conclusions.text: All 21 candidates intersect the retained Angola consumed and same-release full products by positive area; 20 also intersect the corresponding Namibia products. This is a source-geometry observation only.

JRC GSW v1.5 records positive occurrence and 2024 seasonality water-classified pixel centers within all 21 candidate footprints; the exact shoreline/current course, historic channel, and waterbody type remain unresolved.
The 1926 treaty framework and archive catalogue leads are material, but the completed demarcation records needed to establish an exact alignment were not inspected.
The processing cause and any territorial assignment remain unknown; no legal boundary verdict is made.

The JRC Collection 2 transition introduces a documented spatially variable residual co-registration offset, typically sub-pixel but at or above one 30 m pixel in some WRS-2 path/rows; candidate pixel overlays therefore retain this positional limit.

The 1928 joint Kakeri Final Act and 1931 exchange document a historically demarcated 47-beacon line accepted by both governments; the candidates are only coarsely east/south of printed beacon 47 by raw coordinate bounds. The exact candidate-level historical/current Okavango river sector remains unresolved.
